new_statements.quote: Vowel length is generally distinctive, though the duration of a vowel in a given word may vary considerably. Stress normally falls on the final inflectional segment of the word. Unstressed affixes are agglutinative (Layer II) case endings, external tense markers, and enclitic object pronouns.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog records Domari as fixed final stress (final stress, classification fixed-dominant). Matras ELL2 agrees on final placement and adds the domain: stress is final within the stem + Layer I inflection, while Layer II case suffixes, external tense markers and enclitic object pronouns are extrametrical, so surface word-final syllables carrying those affixes are unstressed. The entry does not give secondary stress or weight conditions.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the last syllable of the inflected word, where 'word' excludes a closed set of extrametrical material: Layer II (agglutinative) case endings, the external tense markers (-i-, -a-), and enclitic object pronouns are never stressed, so the stressed syllable is the final syllable of the stem plus Layer I inflection.
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged with 'normally'; the only stated exceptions are the unstressed affix classes (Layer II case endings, external tense markers, enclitic object pronouns), which lie outside the stress domain. No lexical exceptions are listed in this 4-page sketch.
new_statements.identity_note: The ELL2 entry states that 'the only well-documented variety is that of Jerusalem', so its stress statement describes Jerusalem (Palestinian) Domari; Matras's own fieldwork is on that variety.

sources.quote: "Judging by the recorded data, stress assignment in Aleppo Domari is the same as in Palestinian Domari: it falls on the last syllable of the phonological word ... Stress on the first syllable was recorded in certain adverbs of time ... only Layer I case markers ... and bound pronouns are part of the domain of stress ... Layer II markers are never stressed ... Items borrowed from Arabic are integrated into the Domari stress pattern." (cites Matras 1999:14 for Palestinian Domari)
sources.note: Open-access primary fieldwork description with an explicit section 1.3 'Stress' (p. 8): final stress on the phonological word, Layer II case markers and plural /n/ outside the stress domain, initial stress in a few time adverbs and under perfective negation n-. downloaded now; confirms coding and supplies domain detail for the empty 'domain' field (Northern/Aleppo variety).
